title: `go -C * test*` and `go -C * vet*` read-only entries have the same mid-pattern `*` problem

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Raised by the reviewer in round 1 of ork run ork-20261125-203302-a88e for S586. A mid-pattern `*` in `Bash(go -C * test*)` and `Bash(go -C * vet*)` spans the subcommand in ork's matcher model, where `wildcard` turns `*` into `.*` (`internal/agent/claude/pretool.go`; `allowlistMatches` in `internal/engine/perm_test.go:18-28`). The entry `Bash(go -C * test*)` matches `go -C /w get example.com/m test` and `go -C /w mod edit -droprequire=x test`. Both write go.mod from a read-only role. These entries are in `LocalReadOnlyAllowlist` (`internal/engine/perm.go:39`) and in the go implementer preset (`perm.go:107`). S586 pinned every `git -C` entry at launch (`PinGitC`, adj 577, 579, 580) and left `go -C` alone on purpose.

The owner decided to pin `go -C` the same way (session 8d711f67, 2026-11-25). Each `go -C * test*` and `go -C * vet*` entry takes the role's worktree path and becomes `Bash(go -C PATH test*)` or `Bash(go -C PATH vet*)`. A worktree that cannot be pinned drops the `go -C` entries, as it drops the `git -C` entries (adj 580).

The owner also folded in S586 finding 1. The gate's `in.Allow` comes from `ResolvePermission` (`internal/engine/round.go:637-642`), not from `rolePermission`, so it holds the unpinned `git -C *` and `go -C *` templates. For the gate, `in.Allow` feeds only the check-command classification (`checkCommandRunnable`, `internal/engine/brief.go:738`). The gate brief prints no Allowed forms list: that item is printed only for the UI pass and for non-read-only roles (`brief.go:347-361`). The gate's `in.Allow` is therefore pinned to the run's worktree. This is a brief/code mismatch: the brief says the gate shows the template, but the gate only classifies against it.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-25: adj 579 and 580 apply to go -C too; adj 586 keeps the name PinGitC and extends it.

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
All in package `engine` unless noted. The worktree in these tests is `/w`. `PinGitC` keeps its name under adj 586.
- TestReadOnlyAllowlistRefusesGoWritesEndingInTestOrVet (`perm_test.go`, new): for `LocalReadOnlyAllowlist("/w")` and `CloudUIAllowlist("/w")`, each X in test and vet, and each of `go -C /w get example.com/m X`, `go -C /w mod edit -droprequire=x X`, `go -C /w build -o /w/bin X`, `go -C /w install example.com/m X` and `go -C /w generate X`, no entry matches (`matchingEntries`). Today the `go -C * X*` entries match them.
- TestReadOnlyAllowlistPinsGoCToTheWorktree (`perm_test.go`, new): `go -C /w test ./...` and `go -C /w vet ./...` match an entry. `go -C /other test ./...` and `go -C /w/sub test ./...` match none. No entry starts with `Bash(go -C *`. This holds for both lists.
- TestImplementerGoCEntriesRefuseWritesEndingInTestOrVet (`perm_test.go`, new): the go preset passed through `PinGitC(list, "/w")` has no entry that matches the same go write commands for test and vet. `go -C /w test ./...` and `go -C /w vet ./...` do match. No entry starts with `Bash(go -C *`.
- TestPinGitC (`perm_test.go`, change): the input list adds `Bash(go -C * test*)` and `Bash(go -C * vet*)`, and the result holds `Bash(go -C /w test*)` and `Bash(go -C /w vet*)`. The plain `Bash(go test*)`, `Bash(git status*)` and `Read` entries stay as they are. A worktree that is empty, relative, or holds a space, `*`, `,`, a quote or a parenthesis drops every `git -C *` and `go -C *` entry and keeps the rest.
- TestAllowlistMatchesModel (`perm_test.go`, add two cases): `Bash(go -C * test*)` matches `go -C /w get example.com/m test` (true, which documents why the pin is needed), and `Bash(go -C /w test*)` does not (false).
- TestRolePermissionPinsGitCForImplementerAndPart (`perm_test.go`, change): the pinned entries checked for the implementer and a part, with and without grants, also include `Bash(go -C /w test*)` and `Bash(go -C /w vet*)`. No entry other than the grant starts with `Bash(go -C *`. `ResolvePermission` still returns `Bash(go -C * test*)`.
- TestGateBriefClassifiesCheckCommandsAgainstThePinnedImplementerList (`brief_test.go`, new): in a harness run (`routesFor` answers `slicer show` with a Check section holding `go -C W test ./...` and `go -C W/sub test ./...`, W being the worktree), the gate request's brief lists `go -C W test ./...` under "Implementer-runnable Check commands". It does not list `go -C W/sub test ./...` there, because the pinned entry matches only `go -C W`. Today the unpinned template lists both as implementer-runnable.
- TestHappyPathReachesAwaitingApproval (`engine_test.go:311`, TestHappyPathReachesAwaitingApproval, change): the implementer allowlist also holds `Bash(go -C <W> test*)` and none holds `go -C *`.
- TestRetryAllowReachesAResumedStoppedRun (`stoppedresume_test.go:172`, TestRetryAllowReachesAResumedStoppedRun, change): its pinned-base guard also checks that `PinGitC` left no `go -C *` template in `base`.
- TestReadOnlyRoleOnCloudClaudeGetsTheReadOnlyList and TestUIPassStillGetsItsWriteRule (`internal/daemon/runner_test.go`, change through `localReadOnlyToolsFor` at line 286 (localReadOnlyToolsFor)): the helper pins each `Bash(go -C * ` entry to the worktree, or drops it when the worktree is empty. These tests fail until the runner's list has pinned `go -C` entries. TestClaudeRunnerPinsReadOnlyGitCToTheWorktree also asserts `Bash(go -C /work test*)` is present and no entry contains `go -C *`.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/engine/perm.go`, extend the pin function (`PinGitC`) so it handles a second template, `Bash(go -C * `, as well as `gitCTemplate`. Add a `goCTemplate` constant beside `gitCTemplate`. An entry that starts with either template gets the worktree in place of `*` (`Bash(go -C /w test*)`). Every other entry is copied unchanged. The usability test is the same: an absolute worktree where `ShellWord(worktree) == worktree`. When it is not usable, drop every `git -C *` and `go -C *` entry (adj 580). It returns a new slice. Update its doc comment and the `gitCTemplate` comment to name `go -C`.
2. `LocalReadOnlyAllowlist` and `CloudUIAllowlist` already pass their list through the pin function, so their `go -C` entries are pinned once step 1 lands. Update their doc comments to say the go -C entries name the worktree as well (adj 577, `launch.read-only-git-c-form`, and this slice's owner decision).
3. `rolePermission` already pins the implementer's and a part's allowlist with the pin function, so its `go -C` entries are pinned by step 1. Update its comment. `ResolvePermission`, `ImplementerPreset` and `DefaultImplementerAllowlist` keep their signatures and still return the `go -C *` template, because the registry and the settings views show the template. Grants from `ork retry --allow` are not rewritten.
4. In `internal/engine/round.go`, in the gate branch (lines 637-642), set `in.Allow` to the pin function applied to `implementerPerm.Allow` and `rec.Worktree`. The gate then classifies Check commands against the same pinned `git -C` and `go -C` entries the implementer ran with. Grants stay out of this list, as they are today. `internal/engine/speccheck.go`, `specdraft.go` and `carve.go` keep `ResolvePermission` unchanged: they have no run worktree.
5. Write the tests listed under Failing tests and update the existing callers. In `internal/daemon/runner_test.go`, change `localReadOnlyToolsFor` to pin entries that start with `Bash(go -C * ` the way it pins `Bash(git -C * `. Update the `localReadOnlyTemplate` comment to say its `git -C` and `go -C` entries are templates.
6. Update `docs/design.md`:
   - lines 2576-2586 and 2703-2720: say the `go -C` entries, like the `git -C` ones, name the role's worktree at launch, with `Bash(go -C PATH test*)` as the example.
   - lines 2758-2762: the registry still stores the `Bash(go -C * ...)` template.
   - add a sentence that the gate's Check classification uses the pinned list.
7. Run `slicer changelog add S595 --text "..."`. Do not edit `CHANGELOG.md`.
